cover.title: Vendor & Licensing Rationalization
cover.subtitle: Vendor duplication proof, savings case & governance roadmap
cover.meta: Hypothesis H5 · June 2026 · PwC Confidential · Subject to CIO validation
cover.hook: 1,674 vendors serve a $87.2M IT estate — 40 spend-carrying entities buy independently with no IT vendor management framework below Corporate. Consolidating vendor services and licensing onto group standards releases $6.5–8.5M annually at Year-3 run-rate.
cover.source: Source: Culligan Spend Cube June 2026 (reconciled) · Central EAs restated at group value

executiveSummary.title: The situation at a glance
executiveSummary.sectionTitle: Culligan's vendor and license estate is not managed — it is accumulated

rows.detail: 1,674 vendors serve one $87.2M IT estate — 24 business units / 59 legal entities (44 in scope), with spend across 40 entities, buy services and licenses independently. No IT vendor management framework below Corporate. 681 of 728 service vendors locked in a single BU; the same capability spread across ~323 vendors in 34 BUs. 564 software vendors with no group standard. $14.0M in central Microsoft ($6.05M), Salesforce ($7.32M) and SAP ($0.69M) EAs partially unused. ~25–30% of SaaS seats unused (Gartner/Zylo est.). ~83% of IT spend auto-renews without group visibility.

rows.dimension: Why it is a problem — impact on spend
rows.detail: Volume leverage destroyed — a $3.4B enterprise negotiates 1,674 small contracts at BU-local rates. Duplication compounds — the same tools bought in parallel across BUs with no mechanism to retire overlaps. Renewals fragment — ~83% of IT spend auto-renews with no group visibility or challenge. EAs underutilized — $14.0M in central agreements partially unused while BUs buy standalone equivalents. Every renewal cycle without a framework re-locks another year of fragmentation premium.
rows.emphasis: Group CIO authority stops at Corporate — BUs buy independently at every renewal.

rows.detail: $6.5–8.5M gross savings at Year 3 (≈15% blended on ~$47.5M reachable spend). Vendor track $2.1–3.5M on $27.56M addressable services. Licensing track $3.0–6.0M on $45.16M. Wave 1 quick wins $1.0–1.9M self-funding. H5 requires H4 Group CIO mandate before Wave 2.

01. Stand up an IT vendor management framework with a category owner per capability. 02. Name champion/challenger panels per service capability; migrate the 728-vendor services tail. 03. Right-size and extend the central EAs (Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP) — utilization, not new deals. 04. Build a contract renewal calendar immediately — it is the critical-path control. 05. Secure the H4 mandate — H5 cannot be enforced at BU level without it.

methodology.title: How we built the TBM baseline into a consolidation case

steps.title: Build the TBM baseline
steps.detail: Start from the refreshed $87.2M TBM spend, reconciled across 1,674 vendors, 24 BUs and 59 legal entities. Clean vendor name variants (Insight, PTC, U/UKG).

steps.title: Map to capabilities
steps.detail: Map every vendor to the H4 capability model — seven domains and sub-capabilities — by region and BU.

steps.title: Find the overlaps
steps.detail: Within each BU and capability, count how many vendors deliver the same thing.

steps.title: Size & benchmark
steps.detail: Apply industry consolidation benchmarks to the addressable overlap, adjusted for Culligan's fragmentation.

methodology.principles: Everything reconciles to the reconciled TBM baseline ($87.2M / 1,674 vendors). $72.7M addressable (vendor $27.56M + licensing $45.16M). Vendor invoice spend only — internal labour excluded.

validation.title: Stakeholder validation

items.detail: CFO and Group CIO reviewed the spend cube and capability mapping. 37 corrections applied.
Preliminary findings shared with CFO and CEO. Savings ranges, wave sequencing and vendor-count targets endorsed.
Final recommendations confirmed against strategic priorities. Group CIO mandate confirmed as the critical enabler.

validation.finding: Culligan stakeholders confirmed: the scale of fragmentation is greater than previously understood. Leadership endorses the consolidation case and the governance mandate as the non-negotiable first step.

benchmarks.title: Six prioritised levers — benchmarked against Gartner, NPI, Zylo, Flexera, Info-Tech
benchmarks.note: H5 scope: third-party IT services ($27.56M) and software/licensing ($45.16M). Cloud, telecom and hardware excluded from addressable base per reconciled view. ERP rationalization is Wave 3 / H3-dependent.

levers.context: 314 service vendors; 681 of 728 locked in one BU. 80% of spend reachable.
Most immediately renegotiable line in vendor track.
~25–30% seats unused. Ghost-seat recovery — no migration required.
Migrate parallel tools onto group standards (Salesforce EA $7.32M, UKG, etc.).
90 tools across 10 BUs. Wave 3 / H3-dependent — not Year-1 commitment.

currentState.title: Following the money — by region, business unit and capability
currentState.focusUnitsLead: Six highest-spending business units — expand any card to see vendor duplication detail.

focusUnits.name: Corporate
focusUnits.note: Group IT owner — holds the best-negotiated contracts, including the $7.32M Salesforce enterprise agreement and $6.05M Microsoft EA.

currentState.doingWellTitle: What Culligan is already doing well

doingWell.observation: CRM standard is set. EA cost is sunk. Migrating BUs on standalone CRM tools eliminates parallel spend from day one — net positive from the first BU migrated.
doingWell.impact: 89% of CRM spend already on Salesforce — the template for how group-wide agreements should work.

doingWell.observation: Group agreement negotiated and in place. The lever is utilization and tier right-sizing, not a new deal.
doingWell.impact: Recovering ghost seats and right-sizing E3/E5 allocation is the immediate Wave 1 prize.

doingWell.observation: Group ERP anchor exists for Corporate & Flagship — positions SAP as the consolidation target for the fragmented 90-tool ERP tail.
doingWell.impact: Reduces the cost of convergence substantially vs. negotiating a new deal.

doingWell.observation: Mandate extension is a governance decision, not a new hire. The cost and lead time to create the role is already absorbed.
doingWell.impact: The question is scope of authority, not existence — H4 extends the mandate; H5 captures the savings.

doingWell.observation: Group threat monitoring avoids BUs buying endpoint security separately.
doingWell.impact: Already realizing an estimated $1.3–2.3M annual saving — proof of concept for group-standard delivery.

overpaying.area: No IT vendor management framework below Corporate
overpaying.observation: 24 BUs each buy independently. Every consolidation needs BU-by-BU negotiation — the single costliest governance gap.
overpaying.impact: Fragmentation compounds with every acquisition and every renewal.

overpaying.area: No SAM tool — 25–30% of SaaS seats unused
overpaying.observation: $14.0M in central EAs partially unutilized. Seat utilization is invisible without a SAM baseline.
overpaying.impact: Cannot recover what cannot be measured. Zylo or Flexera deployment is a Wave 1 priority.

overpaying.observation: ~83% of IT spend auto-renews without group visibility. Every contract that renews before group frameworks are in place locks in another cycle at BU-local rates.
overpaying.impact: The renewal calendar is the most urgent Wave 1 deliverable — not a reporting tool.

overpaying.area: 681 of 728 service vendors locked in one BU
overpaying.observation: No cross-BU contracts, no group rate cards, no champion panel formalized. Same capability spread across ~323 vendors in 34 BUs.
overpaying.impact: Each BU pays a different price for the same service — volume leverage is zero.

overpaying.area: EAs underutilized — standalone equivalents still being bought
overpaying.observation: Culligan pays for the Salesforce EA and 18 standalone CRMs simultaneously. $0.85M in parallel CRM spend alongside the $7.32M EA is the clearest illustration.
overpaying.impact: Governance absent — every renewal renews at full entitlement, not actual use.

futureState.title: Six moves that unlock $6.5–8.5M a year
futureState.lead: Vendor track ($27.56M) and licensing track ($45.16M) rationalized at group scale. H5 requires H4 governance mandate before Wave 2 vendor consolidation can be enforced.

opportunities.title: IT vendor management framework
opportunities.summary: Category owners, rate cards, renewal calendar and champion/challenger panels across the full estate.
opportunities.why: Wave 1 license recovery self-funds Waves 2 and 3. Governance is the unlock — not procurement alone.

opportunities.title: Service desk / MSP consolidation
opportunities.summary: 728 service vendor relationships → four champion/challenger panels with group rate cards.
opportunities.why: Delivers ITSM standardisation and the foundation for AI-driven automation.

opportunities.title: ERP & finance rationalization
opportunities.summary: 90 ERP tools → one group template (SAP / IFS). H3-dependent — Wave 3 horizon.
opportunities.why: Largest single licensing lever but longest to execute — do not present as Year-1 commitment.

opportunities.title: CRM right-size & standardize
opportunities.summary: Retire 7 minor CRMs; extend the existing $7.32M Salesforce EA to remaining BUs.
opportunities.why: Platform and rate already in place — lowest-risk consolidation lever.

opportunities.title: Telecom & connectivity
opportunities.summary: Telecom partly addressable — carrier contracts constrain near-term consolidation.
opportunities.why: Often overlooked — Quench alone runs 6 UCaaS providers.

opportunities.title: Vendor tail reduction
opportunities.why: Each tail vendor = contract admin, security access point, invoice to process.

deepDives.title: ERP rationalization
deepDives.target: One ERP template (SAP / IFS group standard). Collapse the 90-tool sprawl over 18–36 months — H3-dependent.

deepDives.title: CRM right-size
deepDives.target: Extend the existing $7.32M Salesforce EA and retire 7 minor CRMs across 4 BUs.

deepDives.title: Vendor services consolidation
deepDives.target: Four champion/challenger panels — IT services, managed services, SI, app dev — with group rate cards.

deepDives.title: Licensing rationalization — three levers
deepDives.target: One platform per capability. Recover ghost seats. Extend central-EA chargeback to all BUs.

roadmap.title: Sequence the moves behind a governance mandate
roadmap.lead: License quick wins first (self-funding), then vendor consolidation, then standardize & sustain. Each wave depends on the governance mandate set in Wave 1.

waves.actions: Commission SAM baseline (Zylo or Flexera). Ghost-seat recovery — Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP EAs. Tier right-sizing across top-10 software vendors. Build contract renewal calendar (all 1,674 vendors). Baseline services spend — confirm champion incumbents. Name category owner per service capability.

Formalize 4 champion/challenger panels — group rate cards. Renegotiate top 5 MSP contracts (Insight, Ricoh, Inetum, CGI). Standardize CRM, HRIS, analytics onto group platforms. Launch IT chargeback model for central EAs. Retire parallel tool contracts per standardization map. IT vendor management framework governance live.

ERP rationalization — dependent on H3 IFS template. Retire remaining tail tools (458 below top-10 licensing vendors). Renewal calendar gatekeeping fully operational. SAM governance in steady state — no off-framework buying. Quarterly panel re-tender cadence established.

funding.title: Net economics — cost to achieve
funding.mechanism: Gross $6.5–8.5M run-rate at Year 3. Total cost to achieve $2.0–4.0M one-off over 3 years (SAM tooling, VMO stand-up, panel migration, advisory, internal team). Net annual run-rate saving $3.1–4.5M. Payback 12–18 months. Wave 1 license recovery is self-funding in Year 1.

financialModel.title: H5 savings profile — vendor track $2.1–3.5M · licensing track $3.0–6.0M
financialModel.footnote: Blended ≈15% on reachable spend ($47.5M reachable base per deck reconciliation). Wave savings sum ($4.5–8.2M) is gross build-up by lever; $6.5–8.5M headline applies blended rate. Cost to achieve phased across three waves — ranges are planning-grade pending SAM baseline.

bottomLine.title: Culligan is paying a fragmentation premium on vendor and licensing spend
bottomLine.nextStep: The single highest-leverage action: extend the Group CIO mandate and stand up the IT vendor management framework. H3 application rationalisation is reported separately and netted at programme level.
